seed: Objects of type `ghost` under action ACTION2 with touching neighbours [wall] show mixed outcomes: y x2, x x1, no_change x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: the presence, type or relative position of a neighbouring object. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Player moves 6px per A1-A4, blocked by HUD band/screen edges/wall px; may step onto the wall pressure plate (isolated solid 3x3). First input of a fresh level (counter w=64) is consumed (unconfirmed why).
Wall = rope: plate -> vertical line -> arm + door; while a player/ghost box covers the plate the arm retracts 6px; wall px under layer-1 boxes are cropped.
Ghost hypothesis answered: the ghost does not react to walls; it follows the player trail 2 moves behind and moves only when the player moves (t15 no_change = player blocked).
A5 (player off respawn) toggles ghost mode: respawn at the level's first reached cell, trail restarts [start, respawn], ghost HUD icon prepends, player icons shift +4. Max one ghost / toggle-back is a guess.
Counter loses 1px every 2nd call: parity is hidden state (stateless replay passes 15/35); unobserved: door effect on reaching the gate, A6/A7.
